mu_name_from: Noria's object slot 42, which is the model index: every world but Lorencia runs its objects in one straight sequence, so type N is Object{N+1}.bmd and there is no friendlier name in the client than the number.
sheet_from: Data/Object4/*.OZJ and .OZT, from MuMain, decoded under an nr_ prefix. The prefix is load-bearing for the reason the ground's is: assets/textures is one flat pool for every world, and yellow_jewel.png was already taken by an item.
material_note: itp02: a chain. Grey links on a strip, the gaps between them cut out of the alpha. Noted as a violet blur when it was declared, and given lamplight on that reading; enlarged it is plainly iron.
cutout_from: Each carries a real alpha channel, as decode_texture reports it. Declared rather than detected - three separate attempts to read a cut-out off the art have been wrong, and the client decides it in code.
why_this_one: Object40, Object41, Object42 and Object43 are one thing: all four stand at 18100,10450, a few units apart in height, and together they are the Chaos Machine beside the Chaos Goblin. This is the chain belt.
glow_from: ZzzObject.cpp, MoveObject, case WD_3NORIA, type 42: `Models[o->Type].StreamMesh = 0` and `o->BlendMeshTexCoordU = -(float)((int)WorldTime % 500) * 0.002f`. StreamMesh is the mesh whose texture coordinates take the offset without being blended, so the chain is drawn solid and slides along U - two repetitions a second in MU, where the drum it wraps turns once in two seconds; half a repetition here, because Object40 gears the drum down to a turn in eight (see geared_from) - the mesh's U runs from -25 to 23, so the links are what move and the strip stays put. Not a glow, but the same one number on one material, and Glows is what writes that.
